scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman with long dark wavy hair looks up from dense pink, white and purple flowers toward a golden-brown serpent coiled on a fruit tree. Her head and upper shoulders rise above the plants. A waterfall, stream, distant hills, deer, a lion and a white wading bird fill the sunlit garden.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative watercolor of the serpent addressing the woman before the fruit is taken or eaten. Her attentive gaze echoes the encounter in Genesis 3:1; the flowering foreground naturally puts the rest of her body out of view. The tree species, serpent's branch perch, landscape and animals are artistic details not specified by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a woman with long dark wavy hair speaking to a brown-and-gold serpent coiled around a fruit tree. Her raised empty hand gestures toward hanging red fruit. Dense flowers, ferns and shrubs fill the foreground, with a rocky stream, waterfall and mountains behind.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined garden conversation illustrates the woman's answer about the fruit they may eat. Her open hand gestures toward fruit still on the tree; no fruit is taken or eaten. The flowers, stream, waterfall, colors and serpent's pose are artistic details not specified in this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A long-haired woman raises her left palm near her shoulder as she answers a brown-and-gold serpent beside a fruit tree. Her thumb faces back toward her face. Dense flowers and ferns hide her body; attached fruit, a stream, waterfall, deer and bird fill the sunlit watercolor garden.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures the woman answering the serpent about the forbidden fruit in Genesis 3:3. Her raised empty palm suggests the warning she recounts; no fruit is taken or eaten. The fruit variety, gesture, flowers, animals and garden arrangement are artistic details, not descriptions supplied by this verse. Dense rooted foreground plants incidentally keep her body out of sight before the fruit is eaten.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a long-haired woman looking up at a gold-brown serpent coiled on a fruit-tree branch. Only her head, neck and shoulder tips rise above dense pink and white flowers, leafy plants and ferns. A sunlit garden, rocky stream and waterfall fill the background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined conversation pictures the serpent addressing the woman in Genesis 3:4, before the fruit is eaten. Her attentive expression suggests listening to its denial that they will surely die. The flower bed, waterfall, fruit shape and precise poses are imaginative garden details, not details specified by this verse. No fruit is being taken or eaten.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman with long wavy dark hair looks up at a serpent coiled in a fruit tree, one hand near her chin. Dense flowers and ferns hide her body. Fruit hangs above her, and a stream and small waterfall flow through the sunlit garden. No other person is visible.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Genesis 3:5 records the serpent claiming that eating the fruit will open their eyes and make them like God, knowing good and evil. The woman is shown listening to the serpent while the fruit remains attached to the tree. The garden scene illustrates the conversation, without depicting the promised outcome or the later act of eating.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a long-haired woman offering a whole red-gold fruit to a curly-haired, bearded man. Their heads, shoulder tops and outstretched hands rise above dense flowers and ferns beside a broad tree. Waterfalls, rocks, a deer and a blue bird appear in the sunlit garden.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined garden scene relates to the taking and giving of fruit in Genesis 3:6. It preserves the offering gesture while showing a whole fruit away from both mouths, before any depicted eating. The verse also recounts both eating; this single image does not depict that full sequence. The fruit species, faces, garden details and exact gesture are imaginative, not details specified by the verse.
